title: Normalized realization of integral coefficients and ordinary direct image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$ and $P_n=A/(t^n)$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $T$ on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $C_T=p_T^*\underline A$, $Q_{T,n}=p_T^*\underline{P_n}$, with the continuous-function condensed rings and the specified reduction homomorphisms [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $R_T=\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}_T$ with projections $\pi_{T,n}$, where the underlined finite rings are constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], the internal/section module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], and total derived module direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Use the ring isomorphism $C_T\cong\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}_T$ identifying every finite projection with the actual quotient, the flatness of $C_T$ over $\underline A_T$, and the K-flat resolutions $[C_T\xrightarrow{t^n}C_T]\to Q_{T,n}[0]$ augmented by the actual quotient projection, of [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-resolution-normalization] (with $\pi=t$; its $R_T$ and $S_{n,T}$ are $C_T$ and $Q_{T,n}$ here). Then every $P_n$ is annihilated by $\ell^n$, and $(A,(t))$ satisfies the adic datum hypotheses [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $A$ is Noetherian, $A/(t)$ is additive torsion, and each $P_n$ is finite and perfect in $D(A)$. There exist coefficient models [def-sfb-integral-ambient-coefficient-presentation]: canonical ring isomorphisms $c_T:C_T\cong R_T$ and $c_{T,n}:Q_{T,n}\cong\underline{P_n}_T$ taking each local constant residue class to the same class, with $\pi_{T,n}c_T=c_{T,n}p_T^*(A\to P_n)$; thus $c_T$ is the cited limit isomorphism. The harmless universe lift in that definition takes the class of $a$ to the class of $\operatorname{up}a$.

For every scheme map $f:X\to Y$, these ring identifications respect the canonical inverse-image maps $\alpha_f$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] for $C_T,Q_{T,n}$ and $c_f,c_{f,n}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] for $R_T,\underline{P_n}_T$, and every quotient transition. For any such normalized coefficient models on $X,Y$, the exact internal-module encodings give AmbientEncoding and, at every positive level, FinitePushEncoding [def-sfb-integral-ambient-direct-image-encoding]. Explicitly, the ordinary direct-image comparison is identity on the underlying section groups with their induced scalar actions. The resulting natural isomorphisms of total right derived functors intertwine the universal right-derived units on every complex. Thus they identify the specified ordinary condensed-coefficient direct image with the ordinary $R_T$-module direct image, and the finite internal-module direct image with the fixed-$P_n$ direct image. No completeness, boundedness, properness, or constructibility condition is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-resolution-normalization] with $\pi=t$: $A$ is Noetherian and every $P_n$ is finite with the displayed length-one finite free resolution. This resolution is bounded and consists of finitely generated projectives, so $P_n[0]$ is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. The absolute value in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] restricts to the $\ell$-adic absolute value: $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, hence $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E=(t)$. Write $\ell=ta$ with $a\in A$. For any $\bar b\in P_n$, $\ell^n\bar b=\overline{t^na^nb}=0$; in particular $A/(t)$ is additive torsion. The ideal $(t)$ has the one displayed generator. These verify exactly the arithmetic hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].

The qcqs projection-formula assertion of Lemma 6.5.9 is not applied.

proof.text: For each finite discrete ring $P_n$, [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding] supplies the canonical constant-ring/section-ring isomorphism, normalized on every constant scalar. Its inverse gives $c_{T,n}:Q_{T,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{P_n}_T$, taking each local constant class to itself. The resolution lemma [lem-sfb-integral-quotient-resolution-normalization] gives $\lambda_T:C_T\cong\varprojlim_nQ_{T,n}$ whose projections are the actual quotient maps $q_{n,T}=p_T^*(A\to P_n)$. Put $c_T=(\varprojlim_nc_{T,n})\circ\lambda_T$. Then $\pi_{T,n}c_T=c_{T,n}p_T^*(A\to P_n)$, and $c_T$ is an isomorphism. The definition [def-sfb-integral-ambient-coefficient-presentation] uses targets that are the adic-datum sheaves of $A^\uparrow/(\operatorname{up}t)^n$: sheafified continuous functions on $\pi_0$. [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison] supplies the canonical constants-to-functions isomorphisms $\kappa_n:\underline{A^\uparrow/I^n}\cong(A^\uparrow/I^n)_T$ with $I=(\operatorname{up}t)$, which send each constant to the constant function, and the universe-lift ring isomorphisms $e_n([x])=[x.\mathrm{down}].\mathrm{up}$. Both commute with all quotient transitions. Composing $c_{T,n}$ with $\underline{e_n^{-1}}$ and $\kappa_n$ gives the finite model field, which sends the local constant class of $a$ to the class of $\operatorname{up}a$. Taking the limit of these composites, which commute with transitions, gives the completed field with the projection equation. Thus these are precisely the coefficient-model fields. Any normalized finite comparison agrees locally on constant classes, hence is unique. The jointly monic limit projections then make the completed comparison unique.

proof.text: For a scheme map $f:X\to Y$, the finite inverse-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] sends a constant class to the same class after base change. The maps $\alpha_f$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] are the canonical composition comparisons of inverse images from the point. Consequently the two maps $f^{-1}Q_{Y,n}\to\underline{P_n}_X$ obtained using $c_{Y,n}$ or $c_{X,n}$ agree on constant sections, and hence locally on every section by the normalized constant-ring identification of [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding]. The same calculation for $P_{n+1}\to P_n$ gives compatibility with transitions. At integral level, compose the two maps $f^{-1}C_Y\to R_X$ with $\pi_{X,n}$. The projection equation of step 2 and the projection equation in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] reduce equality to the finite square just checked. Joint monicity of the projections proves the integral square. This uses the stated inverse-image comparison theorem, without assuming that inverse image preserves arbitrary limits.

proof.text: The internal/section equivalences preserve underlying section groups and restrictions identically by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], and are additive exact by [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. Scalar restriction along a ring isomorphism has inverse restriction along its inverse, retaining all additive maps; kernels and cokernels therefore retain the same underlying sheaves. Composing with $c_T$ gives the exact ambient encodings $U_X,U_Y$ specified by [def-sfb-integral-ambient-coefficient-presentation]. At finite level, the same argument with $c_{T,n}$ and the additive exact constant-scalar equivalence of [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-restriction-tensor] gives the specified finite fixed-scalar encodings. All these are equivalences on the whole abelian categories, not just on complete or constructible objects.

proof.text: Write $F=f_{*,\mathrm{int}}$ and $G=f_{*,R}$ for the ordinary ambient direct images. The ordinary internal/section direct-image comparison is supplied by [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]; check its scalar transport here explicitly. On a site object $V$ of $Y$, both $U_YFM$ and $GU_XM$ have section group $M(V\times_YX)$. For $r\in R_Y(V)$ and a section $s$ of this group, their respective actions are $(f_C^\sharp(c_Y^{-1}(r)))s$ and $(c_X^{-1}(f_R^\sharp(r)))s$, with pullback to $V\times_YX$ understood. These are equal by the adjunct of the integral ring square of step 3: $f_C^\sharp c_Y^{-1}=f_*(c_X^{-1})f_R^\sharp$. Thus the identity on section groups is linear, is invertible, and commutes with restrictions and module maps. It gives a natural isomorphism $U_YF\cong GU_X$ with exactly the ordinary identity-on-sections property of [def-sfb-integral-ambient-direct-image-encoding]. This compares the prescribed ordinary functors, whose actions are fixed in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

proof.text: At a positive finite level, start with the ringed $\underline{P_n}$-module direct image and apply the finite fixed-scalar encodings of step 4. Both sides have section group $M(V\times_YX)$; for $b\in P_n$ the induced action on either side is multiplication by the constant class $b$ on that base-changed object. The equality is precisely the finite constant-section square of step 3. The constant-scalar restriction in [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-restriction-tensor] retains the sheaf and its maps, so identity section maps define an invertible natural transformation to the ordinary direct image of sheaves of $P_n$-modules. This is the ordinary square and ordinary normalization required for FinitePushEncoding in [def-sfb-integral-ambient-direct-image-encoding].

proof.text: Apply the right-derived comparison of [lem-derived-exact-equivalence-squares] to the ordinary square of step 5, with its source and target equivalences the exact encodings of step 4 and its right-derived pairs the prescribed total direct images of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. To supply that lemma's unused left-derived data, take $L,L'$ to be zero functors and their left-derived functors to be zero; these are exact, so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] supplies these left-derived pairs. Additivity identifies both ordinary left composites with zero. The resulting right-derived square uses the canonical termwise derived equivalences, via the localization factors in that lemma. Repeat with the two finite exact equivalences and the ordinary finite square of step 6. For either square, if $\alpha_K:V(FK)\to G(UK)$ is its ordinary comparison on a complex, its derived comparison $\beta:DV\,RF\xrightarrow{\sim}RG\,DU$ satisfies $\beta_{QK}\,DV(\eta^F_K)=\eta^G_{UK}\,Q(\alpha_K)$ under those localization factors. The lemma states this equation on every complex, so it gives exactly the normalization in [def-sfb-integral-ambient-direct-image-encoding], hence AmbientEncoding and every FinitePushEncoding. All categories here are ordinary unbounded derived categories, and every preceding construction was for arbitrary $T,f$ and arbitrary modules; no additional scheme or complex hypothesis enters.
